post_topic: Unowned cloud spend and the audit risk hiding inside infrastructure that grew without guardrails
scene_description: A large digital dashboard displaying a chaotic cloud infrastructure map — a tangle of unlabeled AWS or GCP resources, orphaned service accounts, and IAM roles with no clear owner, spread across multiple accounts. In the foreground, Kelvin Davis, a Black/African American man in his late 30s to 40s with short hair greying at the temples and a short neatly trimmed beard, sits at a desk studying the screen with a focused, concerned expression. The tension in the scene is the gap between the scale of the infrastructure sprawl visible on the screen and the absence of any ownership labels, tagging, or guardrails — a system that grew faster than its controls.
